design: Timed follow-up to stage 63 using the same ByteTransformer and AdamW, PADT/EWT official prepared train/dev/test splits, sampled probe and target chunk indices, and eight initialization seeds per language. Compare the three policies afresh within each state on this host; no interim tuning or outcome-dependent restarts.
schedule: For each language/seed, draw 32 warmup training batches of four chunks, then a 20000-by-4 matrix of training candidate indices, then 20000 uniform random positions with the stage-63 generator. Cross-check the first 16 candidate sets with stage 63. Use one common schedule in all nine runs of a state, with independent model/optimizer clones.
policies: Stage-60 timed_run implements random, fresh and reuse4 without changing their decisions or timer. Recompute probe gradient every fourth accepted step for reuse4, every step for fresh. Random applies one uniformly chosen candidate. End each arm at the last accepted update and log a late attempt separately.
order: Enumerate languages then seeds in listed order. Rotate the listed three arms left by (zero-based state index + zero-based repeat) modulo three. Three serial timing repeats per state; each arm has one run at each position.
timing: Single-thread CPU, deterministic Torch algorithms. Three seconds per run including candidate indexing, per-step cloning, probe refreshes and trial updates. Setup, common warmup, schedule, initial clone and held-out loss evaluation are outside the stage-58 timer. Report accepted steps, attempts, actual and overrun seconds, final loss and refresh counts. Disallow schedule exhaustion or missing cases. Log completed rows immediately and preserve interruptions.
primary: Mean Arabic final target loss for reuse4 minus fresh at the common deadline, nats per byte transition; negative favors reuse4. Average three repeats within each paired seed before averaging eight seeds.
secondary: Report English same comparison and reuse4 minus random in each language. Describe losses, accepted updates, paired per-seed differences and their spread. Report magnitude and direction for these states without a pooled cross-language effect, confidence interval, significance test, or adaptive choice of period.
coverage: Two languages, eight seeds, three policies, three repeats: 144 timed runs. Stage 63 measured one-step branch effects along reuse trajectories; its two branches do not provide historical full fresh trajectories. Audit seed/arm pairings, schedule and source hashes, age/refresh logic, deadline adherence and policy-choice prefixes where replay is justified.
scope: Previously examined corpora and fixed 256-chunk test sample per language. Both timing noise and update throughput affect outcomes. The three-second policy clock is not total lifecycle cost.
